source.title: Model Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder Subspace Guided Projections
source.authors: Xu Wang; Zihao Li; Ben-You Wang; Yan Hu; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning and jailbreak prompts on SAE steering and compares them with SSPU; its results identify SAE steering as vulnerable while reporting lower attack accuracy for SSPU.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WMDP–Cyber and utility benchmark outcomes for unlearned models, plus jailbreak evaluation results. Layer-selection and feature-activation analyses are used to choose layers or features, so they are not catalog rows. The paper's discussion of other studies is not recorded as new evidence.
record.test_reason: On gemma-2-2b-it the study measures WMDP-Cyber forgetting and utility for GA, NPO, RMU, SAE steering and the new SSPU. It then runs four jailbreak rewrites of WMDP-Cyber items. The results bear on A (does unlearning hold), E (prompt-only recovery, shown for SAE steering) and F (SSPU proposed as a robust method). There is no fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also quantify their claim: SSPU cuts WMDP-Cyber accuracy 3.22 points below RMU and raises average utility 2.88 points. They argue weight-free SAE steering leaves knowledge encoded and recoverable via prompts.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares several established unlearning methods and proposes SSPU, which uses SAE-derived subspaces to guide parameter updates. Its jailbreak evaluation is not a fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization recovery experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE steering strength α changes forgetting and utility; the paper reports progressively stronger forgetting with increasing |α| and greater utility loss. It also evaluates four different jailbreak prompt formats. Layer 3 was selected for later SAE experiments based on layer-wise results.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: One model is evaluated. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Individual jailbreak values are not transcribed from Figure 3, and the text does not report unmodified-model accuracy under the same jailbreak prompts; therefore attack-specific recovery comparisons are incomplete for RMU and SSPU.

untested.parts: Only one model (gemma-2-2b-it) and only WMDP-Cyber; no WMDP-Bio or other targets; no recovery attacks beyond four jailbreak formats.
Entirely untested; no direction ablation or analysis of blocked access vs deletion.
No other languages, plain rephrasings, in-context information, or optimized/adversarial jailbreaks. No original-model accuracy on the jailbreak sets.
SSPU not tested against relearning, activation ablation, quantization, or stronger adaptive prompt attacks.

missing.what: Averaged jailbreak gaps: SSPU lowers malicious accuracy 13.59 points vs SAE steering and 2.83 vs RMU. This is the only text-stated number bearing on RMU recovery.
SAE steering at α∈{−200,−300,−400}: forgetting grows with |α|, with 15–20% utility loss at −400.

record.verdict_notes: Version codes V1/V5/V6 were remapped to A/E/F. Chance on WMDP four-option MCQ is ~25%, which the paper does not state; SSPU's 23.91 is at chance. Jailbreak results are figure-only and only bounded in the text. There is no original-model baseline on the jailbreak sets, so 'recovery' for SAE steering is relative to its standard-set score. Single model, no uncertainty estimates. Tranche T5 fits because the paper shows SAE steering is shallow while proposing a counter-method (F).

versions.untested_parts: Tested forgetting, utility retention, and jailbreak performance on gemma-2-2b-it for the listed methods. Does not test other models or establish a general result across unlearning methods.
No relearning fine-tuning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or test showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests four WMDP–Cyber jailbreak prompt formats only; does not test other languages, ordinary rephrasings, or in-context information.
Tests SSPU against the four jailbreak prompt formats; does not test its resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization attacks.

relation.reason: It reports unlearning and prompt-only jailbreak results on gemma-2-2b-it.

tranche.reason: Its own results show version A failing or partial for several methods: SAE steering loses all TruthfulQA/GSM8K ability and is recovered by prompts, and GA/NPO collapse GSM8K. That meets the T5 definition (results that a version is wrong or partial).

source_check.notes: The paper's '+2.88% average utility over RMU' does not match Table 1: the three-benchmark means are 47.64 vs 48.70, a gap of 1.06 points (the record's authors_conclusion repeats 2.88 points). Appendix C reports at most 15-20% utility loss at alpha=-400, but Table 1 shows TruthfulQA and GSM8K at 0.00 at alpha=-200. Only one model (gemma-2-2b-it) was tested, with a single seed, and there is no original-model score on the jailbreak sets.

statements.correction: gemma-2-2b-it (2B instruct), the authors' own RMU run (MLP up-proj, layers 1-3): WMDP-Cyber 37.59->27.13; MMLU 56.83->56.00; GSM8K 43.75->39.80. Four jailbreak rewrites on RMU: per-set values figure-only; text says SSPU is 2.83% lower than RMU.
statements.problem: This study (r13, r14) fits 'near-chance WMDP with MMLU kept'. But the stated conditions (6-8B models; the only attack is enhanced GCG) exclude it. It is a 2B model, and its RMU was also hit with four prompt rewrites.
The numbers are right, but the heading 'clean MMLU hides losses' implies GA/NPO kept MMLU. In fact MMLU falls about 6 and 4.5 points. The record's verdict for GA/NPO is limits_scope, not challenges.
